mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes ML 270 CDI or 320 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt OM647 engine for the ML 270 CDI costs £2,000-£2,600 supply-only; a rebuilt OM648 engine for the ML 320 CDI costs £2,200-£3,000 supply-only. Fitting adds £800-£1,500 depending on complexity - inline diesel engines are relatively accessible.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of injector seal failure on a Mercedes ML 270 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Diesel fumes in the cabin and carbon buildup around the injectors are the classic warning signs on the OM647 engine. The copper sealing washers fail over time, allowing combustion gases to escape. If ignored, injectors can seize in the head.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes ML 270 CDI or 320 CDI engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the OM647 and OM648 are among Mercedes' most durable diesel engines - the OM647 inline-five and OM648 straight-six are renowned for longevity, with many exceeding 200,000 miles. Regular maintenance and proactive attention to known issues like injector seals and EGR systems are key to their long life.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes ML 270 CDI and 320 CDI engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained OM647 and OM648 engines routinely reach 200,000+ miles before major work is needed. One owner reported 200,000 miles with only minor issues like injector seals and ancillaries.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes ML 270 CDI or 320 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the M Class is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt OM647 costs £2,000-£2,600 - comparable to the value of a £3,000-£8,000 vehicle, making it a justifiable investment for well-maintained examples.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes ML 270 CDI or 320 CDI need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies low-SAPS oil meeting MB 229.51 - typically 5W-30. The OM647 requires approximately 7 litres; the OM648 requires approximately 8 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz M Class 270 CDI/320 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The ML 270 CDI launched with the W163 generation in 1999 as Mercedes' first premium SUV diesel, powered by the OM647 2.7-litre inline-five - a robust, turbocharged engine delivering 163hp. In 2002, the ML 320 CDI joined the range with the OM648 3.2-litre straight-six diesel, offering a smoother, more powerful 224hp and representing the pinnacle of W163 diesel refinement before the W164 generation introduced V6 architecture.

milestones.description: OM647.961, 2.7L inline-five diesel, 163hp @ 4,200rpm (ML 270 CDI, W163 launch)
End of W163 production; OM647 and OM648 replaced by OM642 V6 diesel in W164 generation

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz M Class 270 CDI/320 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The M Class 270 CDI's OM647 inline-five and the 320 CDI's OM648 straight-six are among Mercedes' most durable diesel engines - robust, simple, and capable of 200,000+ miles with proper maintenance. However, both have well-documented weak points that become more pronounced with age and mileage. The OM647 is prone to injector copper seal leaks, while the OM648 can suffer from EGR clogging and oil cooler seal degradation. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: OM647 Injector Copper Seal Leak - The 2.7 CDI's Most Common Annoyance
problems.rootCause: The copper sealing washers under the injectors can fail over time, allowing combustion gases to escape past the injector body. The leaking gases bake into a hard, tar-like carbon crust around the injector - known as "Black Death." This creates diesel fumes in the cabin and a messy engine bay.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace copper sealing washer, clean injector bore, leak-off test
repairOptions.longevity: If caught early before injector seizes

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all five copper sealing washers, clean injector bores, new hold-down bolts
repairOptions.longevity: If multiple injectors are leaking or preventative maintenance

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Specialty pullers, head work, injector seat machining
repairOptions.longevity: If injector has seized and requires extraction

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM647 with new injectors, seals, and EGR components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If injector damage has caused cylinder or head damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 1999-2005 ML 270 CDI or ML 320 CDI is worth approximately £3,000-£8,000 depending on mileage and condition. These classic SUVs sit in a value band where repair decisions require careful consideration - a full engine replacement may approach or exceed the vehicle's value for higher-mileage examples.
problems.recommendation: Injector seal leaks on the OM647 are common but usually not urgent. If you notice diesel fumes in the cabin or see carbon buildup around the injectors, have a specialist inspect the seals immediately. Caught early, resealing an injector is a £120-£250 per cylinder job. Caught late, extracting a seized injector can require specialty pullers and head work. On an ML 270 CDI worth £3,000-£8,000, preventative injector seal replacement is always the better investment.

problems.rootCause: The OM648's EGR valve can become clogged with carbon deposits, especially on vehicles used for short journeys or with extended service intervals. This causes rough idle, surging, and hesitation - a common complaint on these otherwise reliable engines.

problems.recommendation: EGR clogging on the OM648 is a maintenance issue, not a fundamental engine failure. If caught early, cleaning the EGR valve at a specialist is a cost-effective solution. If the valve requires replacement, specialist pricing of £250-£500 is significantly lower than dealer rates. Regular use of quality diesel and occasional Italian tune-ups can help prevent carbon buildup.

problems.group: OM647/OM648 Cold Start & Power Loss Issues
problems.h4: OM647/OM648 Cold Start & Power Loss Issues - The Electrical and Fuel System Traps
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes M Class ML 270 CDI (OM647), ML 320 CDI (OM648), 1999-2005
problems.rootCause: Cold start problems on both OM647 and OM648 engines can be caused by air ingress into the fuel system overnight, often from degraded seals or hoses. Loss of power or limp mode on the OM647 can also result from a defective 10A fuse for the engine control unit, triggering multiple fault codes.

problems.recommendation: Cold start problems on these classic diesels are often simple fixes - air in the fuel lines from degraded seals is a common culprit. For power loss issues, check the 10A fuse for the engine control unit before assuming major component failure. If the engine starts and runs but suffers from intermittent power loss, a simple fuse replacement may resolve the issue.
